items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: For instance, I think Will Hines could probably play ragtime if he wanted to.

ctx.x: That's kind of brings us into my next point very naturally. You're known internationally, basically, as a ragtime pianist. Do you think that this is an apt description of your style? I'm sure it limits your range to call you a ragtime pianist. What do you think of the tag personally, though?

Yes, I think the tag ragtime is sort of put me in a certain category that has been hard for me to overcome from lots of directions. The people who traditionally like ragtime don't like to hear me play anything else. And, of course, I don't play in a strict progressive sense. That's okay. But I would say that just saying that I'm a ragtime piano player, while I feel very flattered to have been included in this category with many of the real ragtime greats, I think I went a little beyond that because I didn't stop…

Certainly, I don't see any harm in keeping up with some of the things that are going on. I think it's kind of ironic that you say the people who like to hear you play ragtime like little else, and it must cause a problem on a job, because most people don't come to the night to the average cocktail lounge to hear ragtime, which is a problem. That's right. Would you like to play more ragtime in the cocktail work where you're limited to playing very little of it? You often feel the urge to play more, even though…
